title: AI Techlead
description:
At a glance
Our AI team builds GenAI applications that go into production at one of the Netherlands' largest banks. Voice agents handling thousands of contact center calls. AI lending assistants supporting lenders in writing credit proposals. Agentic workflows that actually make it to users.
We don't stop at prototypes. We build, ship, measure, iterate, and do it fast. As an
AI Tech Lead
, you set the technical direction across these initiatives and stay close enough to the code to keep that pace honest. If you've got 7+ years of engineering experience, a serious track record of shipping AI in production, and you're looking to lead at a scale most companies won't give you for years, read on.
Your job
You set the technical direction on GenAI initiatives that span the bank: from the first conversation with a business team through to production and beyond. You decide how things get built, you build with the team, and you make sure the right things actually get done in a complex organisation. Your focus shifts with the use case: backend, frontend, from leveraging LLM’s to agentic. You own outcomes, not just architecture diagrams. You work directly with the people whose problems you're solving, and you bring the rest of the team along.
Concretely, you'll:
Set the technical direction for GenAI solutions across banking use cases: Voice AI, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, document intelligence.
Drive initiatives end-to-end through a complex organisation: align stakeholders, unblock teams, make the calls that need to be made.
Co-create use cases with business counterparts: you understand the problem, not just the technology, and you shape what gets built.
Stay hands-on: design and write the hard parts if required.
Own architecture and technical quality across multiple workstreams: trade-offs, patterns, what we standardise on, what we don't.
Work with Agents, plain LLMs, code, Databricks and whatever the right tool is for the job.
Raise the technical bar of the team: code reviews, design reviews, knowledge sharing, coaching mediors and juniors.
Working environment
You'll be part of a 25+ person AI team inside ABN AMRO's Innovation department. We operate with a startup mindset within a bank that serves millions of customers and employs thousands of individuals: fast feedback loops, direct lines to business leadership, and real deployment at scale. Amsterdam, hybrid.
Your profile
We don't hire on CV titles. We hire on what you've shipped and what you've led. The team includes people who came through software engineering, data science, infra — what they share is proven AI expertise and a bias for building over theorising. As a tech lead, you bring the same plus the ability to take an ambiguous problem and a group of strong engineers and turn it into something running in production.
What you've done:
Led the technical side of AI or software initiatives end-to-end: you've owned the architecture, made the hard calls, and shipped.
Built and deployed AI applications using LLMs, RAG, agents, fine-tuning, voice AI, or equivalent (at production scale, with real users).
Written Python that runs in production: you're a developer, not a notebook user, and you still enjoy writing the code.
Worked with cloud infrastructure: Azure preferred, AWS or GCP also fine.
Operated inside a complex organisation (or built the muscle elsewhere) and got things done across teams, not just within one.
How you work:
You take ambiguous problems, set a direction, and bring people with you (without waiting for permission).
You have strong technical opinions, formed through experience, and you're willing to defend them and change them.
You're as interested in the business problem as in the technical solution.
You explain your decisions clearly to people who don't share your context (engineers, business, leadership).
You follow the GenAI field closely because you're genuinely curious, not because you have to.
You've built something on the side (a tool, a project, a contribution) that shows you don't wait to be told what to learn.
We are offering
We believe it is important to be a good employer. Joining us means stepping into a role with impact, supported by excellent employment conditions that foster your job satisfaction, development, and wellbeing. In addition, we offer:
An attractive gross monthly salary based on a 36‑hour work week, including holiday allowance and a flexible benefit budget which adds up to a range of €65.000 to €93.000 a year based on a 36-hour week (40 hours possible, pro-rated)
An excellent pension scheme, ensuring that you are well prepared for the future.
Flexibility in working: working from home is possible in consultation with your team and depending on your role. We will provide an ergonomic home office setup for you.
Plenty of room for relaxation with five weeks of vacation per year, supplemented by two mandatory days off. You can also purchase up to four additional weeks of vacation annually.
Five “Banking for better days”: extra days off that you can use for personal development or volunteer work.
Personal development is key: you receive a development budget of €1,000 per year, which can accumulate up to €3,000.
An annual public transport pass with free public transportation throughout the Netherlands for both business and private use.
You can find more information about our employment conditions and salary scales in our Collective Labour Agreement (CLA), which applies to this vacancy.
Interested?
No motivation letter. Please answer these two questions instead:
Tell us about an AI initiative you led: what did you build, what calls did you make as the technical lead, and what did you learn when it hit production (or real users)?
What's the most interesting thing you've built or experimented with in AI in the last six months? Why does it matter to you?

Je krijgt de ruimte om te experimenteren, je verder te ontwikkelen en met jouw inzichten het verschil te maken.
Werkomgeving
Wij zijn het Advanced Analytics & AI Center of Expertise (AA&AI CoE), onderdeel van het Transaction Banking Data Domain. Onze missie is om maximale waarde te halen uit transactionele bankdata en zo bij te dragen aan betere besluitvorming binnen de bank. Ons domein omvat een breed portfolio aan producten en diensten, zoals rekeningen, betaalkaarten, spaarproducten, verzekeringen, open banking API’s, handelsfinanciering en digitale oplossingen zoals Apple Pay en Google Pay. Ook de bijbehorende verkoop-, bedrijfs- en risicomanagementprocessen vallen hieronder. Met datagedreven inzichten spelen we een belangrijke rol in het versterken van de resultaten van de bank.
We zetten advanced analytics en nieuwe technologieën (zoals Generative AI) in om waarde uit data te halen. Denk aan het ontdekken van trends in productgebruik en transacties, het voorspellen van ontwikkelingen, het optimaliseren van processen en het verbeteren van prestaties. title: Internship | Developing an Unified Software Environment for the Automated Visual Inspection System
description:
About this position
A previous internship delivered several software tools that significantly improved the usability of the automated visual inspection system. These tools support profile generation, profile installation, report generation, and rapid testing of inspection settings. However, users still need to switch between multiple scripts and interfaces, which increases complexity and the risk of user errors.
This internship focuses on developing a unified software environment that integrates these separate tools into a single user-friendly application. The solution should simplify the inspection workflow, hide the underlying file structure from operators, and clearly separate the roles and responsibilities of operators and process engineers.
What will be your role?
You will analyze the current collection of support tools and map the existing inspection workflow.
You will design and develop a software application that combines profile management, installation, report generation, and testing functionality into a single interface.
You will improve usability by reducing complexity and making the underlying file structure largely invisible to users.
You will implement safeguards that reduce the risk of user errors while maintaining flexibility for process engineers.
You will work closely with engineers and operators within Optics Manufacturing to validate requirements and test the developed solution in a practical environment.
What we expect from you
You are currently enrolled in an HBO program in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Technical Informatics, or a comparable technical field.
You have experience with software development and programming.
You enjoy designing user-friendly software solutions and translating user requirements into practical applications.
You have strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
You communicate clearly and can collaborate with different stakeholders.
You are interested in industrial automation, software architecture, and quality-driven engineering environments.
What you'll get in return
An internship at TNO means working in an environment where substance and impact are central. You will become part of a knowledge organisation where research and practice come together, and where experts collaborate on solutions to current societal and technological challenges.
Your internship is a period in which you can discover what suits you, where your strengths lie and what you would like to learn next. You are part of a professional working environment, gain insight into how things work in practice, and have the opportunity to build experience that goes beyond this internship alone. For many students, an internship is therefore also a first step in discovering whether TNO could be a potential next step after graduation.
In addition, we offer you:
A professional and innovative internship environment in which you actively contribute to societal and technological challenges, working alongside leading experts in your field.
Personal and dedicated supervision, with focus on your learning objectives, development and study assignment.
Room to develop: you gain relevant work experience, develop both your subject‑specific and professional skills, and build a valuable network.
Use of a laptop and the facilities you need to perform your work effectively.
A monthly internship allowance of € 615 for a full-time internship, for MSc, BSc and vocational education (MBO) students.
Up to eight hours of leave per internship month for a full-time internship, allowing you to balance your internship with your studies and personal life.
A contribution towards travel expenses if you are not entitled to a student travel card.
A free membership to
Jong TNO:
the network for young colleagues, where you can meet other TNO colleagues and participate in sports activities, professional and personal development activities, and social events such as the annual ski trip.
TNO as an employer
Our people are at the heart of TNO. Their curiosity, expertise and entrepreneurial mindset make it possible to deliver high-impact research and innovations that contribute to society’s sustainable wellbeing and prosperity. That is why we invest in an inspiring and
inclusive working environment
where colleagues can excel, have autonomy and continue to grow.
Your talent and ambition have every opportunity to flourish at TNO. You work with experts (both within and beyond TNO), have access to advanced technology and the freedom to explore, experiment and innovate. Our strength lies in independence, reliability and collaboration. We find each other in wonder and ingenuity. We are driven to push boundaries. By working with businesses and government, and by connecting different perspectives, we strengthen our innovative capability and create responsible, meaningful results.
At TNO, we believe
this is our time
to help society, government and business move forward faster. Together with driven colleagues, you turn knowledge into concrete innovations or ventures that truly make a difference by combining the power of science and entrepreneurship. And in doing so, you make your mark on our time.
The selection process
You can apply for this internship position until the 14th of August, 2026. After submitting your application, you will receive a confirmation by email.
TNO will arrange an appropriate internship agreement. If you have any questions about the content of the internship or the application procedure, you can contact the person listed below.
If you start an internship with us, we will also ask you to provide a Certificate of Conduct (VOG).
Important to know before applying:
Before the start of the internship, an internship agreement must be signed. For students enrolled at a Dutch university or university of applied sciences, TNO uses the
UNL-template
, supplemented with several TNO‑specific agreements. For students from foreign educational institutions and MBO (secondary vocational education) programmes, the TNO internship agreement applies. TNO does not sign any other internship agreements.
Before the start of the internship, the educational institution will need to confirm in writing that:
you are enrolled at the educational institution for the duration of the internship, and;
the internship forms part of your study programme.
The confirmation of educational institution takes place by signing the UNL template or forms prepared by TNO.
Interns at TNO must have a registered residential address in the Netherlands at the start of the internship. Carrying out internship activities from abroad is not possible.
Are you an international student? Please note that you must have a BSN (Dutch citizen service number) before the start of your internship. Applying for a BSN can take several weeks, so make sure to start this process well in advance.

title: Software Engineer Maritime Signature Systems
description:
About this position
Help make our naval vessels invisible to the enemy with your software? Do you want to make a real impact by helping the Royal Netherlands Navy prepare for the future? Join TNO in The Hague as a Software Engineer!
Within the Autonomous Systems & Decision Support division, TNO develops technologies for autonomous systems, sensors, and decision support with direct relevance to Defence. The Integrated Mission Management department translates this expertise into practical software solutions for complex operational environments, including those on board naval vessels.
In this role, you will contribute to, among other things, maritime signature management systems: software that helps predict and influence the visibility and vulnerability of ships. By doing so, you support the Royal Netherlands Navy in remaining effective, safe, and deployable under future operational conditions.
What will be your role?
As a Software Engineer, you will work on one or more projects within the department. In any case, you will become part of the highly motivated development team focused on signature management. Within this team, you will collaborate with scientific staff on a maritime signature management system that helps predict and influence the visibility of ships and their vulnerability to threats.
While the scientific staff focuses on the models and their underlying scientific principles, you will ensure that this knowledge is translated into robust, maintainable, and testable software for operational use aboard current and future naval vessels. You will develop a solid understanding of the key concepts behind the models and be able to connect them to the operational needs of the customer.
The team follows a SAFe/Scrum-based way of working. Within this environment, you will make a tangible contribution to a shared mission: making signature management capabilities available to the Royal Netherlands Navy fleet.
What we expect from you
We are looking for a Software Engineer who is energized by building reliable software for complex, technically challenging applications. You enjoy collaborating with scientific staff and helping to transform their models and prototypes into robust, maintainable, and testable software suitable for operational use. Your strength lies in professionalizing software, safeguarding quality, and ensuring that research results can be applied reliably in practice.
We are looking for candidates with the following background and qualities:
A degree or demonstrable background in Software Engineering.
The ability to work independently, take ownership, and perform effectively as part of a team.
A results-oriented and customer-focused mindset, with the ability to thrive in a multidisciplinary environment.
Strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical decisions in a clear and understandable way.
We are looking for people with knowledge of:
Python and/or C++; experience with Java is a plus.
Software development for Linux-based systems, specifically Debian and Red Hat.
Software quality, testability, maintainability, and software testing techniques.
Software parallelization.
Experience with the following is considered a plus:
GitLab CI/CD pipelines.
Docker and Kubernetes.
Requirements:
You are available for at least 32 hours per week.
You are fluent in English; Dutch is a plus.
You are willing to work on-site at TNO in The Hague at least three days per week.
Your commandment of the English (and preferably also the Dutch) language both verbally and in writing is excellent (C1 Level).

Challenging and varied work with a real impact. And plenty of opportunities as, at TNO, you are in charge of shaping your career. We offer a gross monthly salary between € 3,500,- and € 5,000,- (based on your knowledge and experience), 8% holiday pay, a 13
th

33 days annual leave plus a flexible holiday that can be used on a cultural, religious, or otherwise important day of your choosing (on a full-time basis).

respectful, inclusive, and equitable work environment
where every employee can flourish, with various initiatives such as
Jong TNO

mobility plan

Great social events with your team and other

. That’s how you will get to know a lot of people really quickly.
Flexible working hours, the possibility to work parttime (32 or 36 hours) and the possibility of working from home.
A good pension scheme.
